captions.caption: Electric charges, such as the positive charge (on the left) and negative charge (on the right) shown here, create an electric field around them. Parts of the field are shown in this image as field lines: lines that begin or end at one of the charges. These lines are directed, as indicated by the arrows along each line. Place a positively-charged test particle on one of the lines, and it will feel an acceleration in the direction of the line. A negatively-changed particle will feel an acceleration in the opposite direction to the direction of the line.
captions.alt_text: Positive/negative electric charge as red/blue circles, with lines and arrows that point away from/towards them
